Offload P0/P1 second rotate to the PRMT byte-permute pipe: derive rotl(x,17)=rotl(rotl(x,9),8) and rotl(x,23)=rotl(rotl(x,15),8) as prmt.b32 (selector 0x2103 = rotl8) instead of a 2nd shf, in new vector helpers sm3_p0_prmt/sm3_p1_prmt (inc_hash_sm3.cl) called from SM3_P0/SM3_P1 macros. Value-identical (byte rotate = bit rotate by 8; selftest PASS). +3.2% vs baseline 7245.9 (7480.0, confirm 7477.6), FAR beyond noise band (all 5 prior no-op discards were 7250-7294). FIRST KEEPER for SM3: overturns the prior roofline conclusion. Root cause: prmt executes on a distinct issue port from shf.l.wrap on sm_86 (RTX 3090), so moving 1 of every 2 rotates in P0 (64x/hash) and P1 (51x/hash) off the SHF-saturated INT/ALU datapath (~115 of 561 shf) directly relieves the #1 bottleneck. Same instruction count (1 shf+1 prmt+1 LOP3 vs 2 shf+1 LOP3) so no regression risk; the latency serialization (r17<-r9) that sank the SHF-only sharing exps #4/#5 is hidden because a3 is throughput-bound. Next: same trick on rotl(d,7)/rotl(c,15) has no by-8 partner to share, but exploring prmt for rotl16/rotl24-adjacent state rotates may yield more.
